title: Exact bar resolutions and cone connecting maps
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a small category and $R$ a commutative ring. Write $\mathcal A_{\mathcal E,R}=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{op},\operatorname{Mod}_R)$; it is the module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] for the constant ring on the topology generated by singleton identities [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Derived categories and cochain complexes mean [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Here left $V$-acyclic means that the canonical comparison $LV(M[0])\to V(M)[0]$ is an isomorphism for the object $M$ in question. For $U\in\mathcal E$ and an $R$-module $M$, put $L_U(M)(V)=\bigoplus_{a:V\to U}M$, with restriction along $b:W\to V$ sending $(a,m)$ to $(ab,m)$. For $F\in\mathcal A_{\mathcal E,R}$, let $B_{\mathcal E,R}(F)^{-n}=\bigoplus_{U_n\to\cdots\to U_0}L_{U_n}(F(U_0))$ for $n\ge0$, with zero positive terms. On evaluation at $V$ its generators are $(V\xrightarrow a U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$. The face $d_j$ deletes $U_{n-j}$, composing adjacent arrows (including $a$ when $j=0$); the last face restricts $x$ along $U_1\to U_0$. Use differential $\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^jd_j$ for $n>0$, and augmentation $a_F(a:V\to U_0,x)=F(a)x$ in degree zero. Put $C_{\mathcal E,R}=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal E^{op}}$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Write $K_{\mathcal E,R}(F)^{-n}=\bigoplus_{U_n\to\cdots\to U_0}F(U_0)$, zero in positive degrees, with differential $\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^jd_j$ deleting $U_{n-j}$, composing at internal vertices and restricting the coefficient only for $j=n$. Assume that for every $F\in\mathcal A_{\mathcal E,R}$ the augmentation $a_F$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $B(F)$ is termwise left $C_{\mathcal E,R}$-acyclic (and, in the reindexing clause below, the same hypotheses for every presheaf on $\mathcal D$ and for $LC_{\mathcal D,R}$, and termwise left $C_{\mathcal D,R}$-acyclicity of $u_!B(F)$), and the total left derived colimit $LC_{\mathcal E,R}$ is defined everywhere [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization] and triangulated with its canonical comparison $\varepsilon$. Define $m_F=Q(b_F)\varepsilon_{B(F)}LC_{\mathcal E,R}(Qa_F)^{-1}$, where $b_F:CB(F)\cong K(F)$ is the identity on coefficient generators. For every objectwise short exact sequence $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$, the sequences of $B$-complexes and $K$-complexes are degreewise short exact. Their cone roofs identify the connecting map $QK(F'')\to QK(F')[1]$ with the image by $LC_{\mathcal E,R}$ of the connecting map $F''[0]\to F'[1]$, conjugated by $m_{F''}$ and $m_{F'}[1]$ and the shift comparison of $LC$. Explicitly, for any short exact sequence of complexes $A\xrightarrow i B\xrightarrow p C$ occurring here, $q:\operatorname{Cone}(i)\to C$, $(b,a)\mapsto p(b)$, is a quasi-isomorphism and the connecting map is the roof $C\xleftarrow q\operatorname{Cone}(i)\xrightarrow{-\operatorname{pr}}A[1]$ with the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its kernel is identified with $A^r\oplus A^{r+1}$, differential $(a,a')\mapsto(da+a',-da')$, contracted by $(a,a')\mapsto(0,a)$. A morphism of such short exact sequences induces the cone map $(b,a)\mapsto(f_Bb,f_Aa)$ commuting with $q$ and $-\operatorname{pr}$. Consequently any augmentation-compatible maps of these bar-resolution sequences, including maps to a precomposed bar-resolution sequence for any small category $\mathcal D$ and functor $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$, give commuting squares with the connecting maps after applying colimit and the derived comparisons. For any homomorphism $R_0\to R$ of commutative rings, these assertions also hold after the exact restriction to $R_0$-module complexes.

proof.text: Evaluation of the given objectwise short exact sequence at each $U_0$ is short exact. By exactness of $L_U$ and small sums in [lem-trf-representable-sum-shriek-acyclic], applying the displayed formula for $B^{-n}$ gives a short exact sequence of presheaves in every degree. Applying exactness of small sums of modules to the formula for $K^{-n}$ gives the corresponding assertion for $K$. The induced maps commute with each face, since the coefficient maps are natural, so these are short exact sequences of complexes. The augmentations commute with these maps by $h_VF(a)=G(a)h_{U_0}$.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), exactness assertion; arbitrary-module representable refinement

proof.text: For any degreewise short exact sequence $A\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{p}C$, set $T=\operatorname{Cone}(i)$. The convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $d_T(b,a)=(db+i(a),-da)$, so $q(b,a)=p(b)$ is a chain map and is surjective in each degree. Its kernel is identified by $(x,y)\mapsto(i(x),y)$ with $A^r\oplus A^{r+1}$ and differential $(x,y)\mapsto(dx+y,-dy)$. The degree $-1$ map $h(x,y)=(0,x)$ satisfies $dh(x,y)+hd(x,y)=(x,y)$: the two terms are $(x,-dx)$ and $(0,dx+y)$. Every kernel cocycle is therefore a boundary. The long exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], applied to $0\to\ker q\to T\to C\to0$, shows that $H^r(q)$ is an isomorphism for all $r$. Thus $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

The cone triangle of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] has last arrow $-\operatorname{pr}:T\to A[1]$. Since $qi=p$, replacing its third object by $C$ through the isomorphism $Qq$ gives the distinguished short-exact-sequence triangle with connecting arrow $\delta_S=Q(-\operatorname{pr})(Qq)^{-1}$. This proves the asserted roof, including its minus sign. If $f=(f_A,f_B,f_C)$ is a map of short exact sequences, the diagonal map $t(b,a)=(f_Bb,f_Aa)$ commutes with the cone differentials because $f_Bi=i'f_A$. Direct evaluation gives $q't=f_Cq$ and $(-\operatorname{pr}')t=f_A[1](-\operatorname{pr})$. Inverting $Qq,Qq'$ yields $\delta_{S'}Qf_C=(Qf_A)[1]\delta_S$.

source.place: Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), proof and functorial cone computation

proof.text: Put $V=C_{\mathcal E,R}$. It is additive and right exact: the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] identifies maps from $VH$ into $N$ with natural maps $H\to\underline N$, so $V$ is left adjoint to the constant functor; it preserves cokernels and finite sums by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. The presheaf category has enough projectives by [lem-trf-representable-sum-shriek-acyclic]. The complexes $B(F)$ are bounded above (zero above degree zero), and are termwise left $V$-acyclic by hypothesis. Thus [lem-trf-bounded-above-acyclic-derived-computation] gives an isomorphism $e_F=\varepsilon_{B(F)}LV(Qa_F)^{-1}$. Moreover $VB(F)\cong K(F)$: colimit sends each $L_U(M)$ to $M$ identically on coefficients by [lem-trf-representable-sum-shriek-acyclic], and preserves the sums. Each face then becomes exactly the stated face of $K$. Hence $m_F=Qb_Fe_F$ is an isomorphism, natural for the augmentation maps in step 1.

source.place: Tags 05S9 and 06XN; dual of Tag 015E; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08PG

proof.text:
We use the canonical shift comparison $\sigma_X:LV(X[1])\cong LV(X)[1]$. Here its compatibility with $\varepsilon$ is essential. Applying the pointwise Kan bridge [lem-pur-left-derived-defined-pointwise-kan-bridge] to the everywhere-defined denominator diagrams identifies their canonical comparison with the counit of the pointwise right Kan extension of $QV$ along $Q$; the assembly statement [new-everywhere-defined-derived-functors] supplies its universal transformation. The functors $Q$ and $QV$ commute with shifts, and the latter is exact on the homotopy category by [lem-trf-additive-homotopy-triangulated] and the exact localization in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Consequently [lem-pur-right-kan-extension-coherent-shift] gives the canonical coherent shifts with
$$\varepsilon_X[1]\,\sigma_{QX}=\varepsilon_{X[1]},$$
where the termwise and localization shift identifications are understood. This fixes the shift used below; it is the canonical derived structure, rather than an independently selected shift isomorphism.

Let $S_B$ be the short exact sequence $B(F')\xrightarrow{i}B(F)\to B(F'')$ and $T=\operatorname{Cone}(i)$. Additivity of $V$ identifies $VT$ with $\operatorname{Cone}(Vi)$ and $Vq$ with the cone quotient for the degreewise exact sequence $VS_B$ (step 1 and $b$). Denote its boundary by $\delta_{VS_B}$ and the boundary of $S_B$ by $\delta_B$. Naturality of $\varepsilon$ at $q$ and $r=-\operatorname{pr}$ gives
$$Q(Vq)\varepsilon_T=\varepsilon_{B(F'')}LV(Qq),\qquad Q(Vr)\varepsilon_T=\varepsilon_{B(F')[1]}LV(Qr).$$
Since $Q(Vq)$ and $Qq$ are invertible by step 2, the roof formula and step 5 give
$$\delta_{VS_B}\varepsilon_{B(F'')}=Q(Vr)Q(Vq)^{-1}\varepsilon_{B(F'')}=\varepsilon_{B(F')}[1]\sigma_{QB(F')}LV(\delta_B).$$
This computation uses no exactness of $V$ on arbitrary short exact sequences, and no uniqueness claim for a triangulated boundary.

source.place: Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), cone roofs; canonical comparison naturality

proof.text:
Write $\delta_0:F''[0]\to F'[0][1]$ for the boundary of the original sequence. Applying step 3 to the augmentation map of short exact sequences gives
$$\delta_0\,Qa_{F''}=Qa_{F'}[1]\,\delta_B.$$
Apply $LV$ and use naturality of its shift comparison. Multiplying the identity of step 6 on the right by $LV(Qa_{F''})^{-1}$ and on the left by the shifted coefficient identification $Qb_{F'}[1]$ now gives
$$\delta_K m_{F''}=m_{F'}[1]\,\sigma_{F'[0]}\,LV(\delta_0),$$
where step 3 for the isomorphism $b$ identifies $\delta_K$ with the boundary for the exact sequence of $K$-complexes. Cancelling the isomorphism $m_{F''}$ proves precisely the claimed conjugation formula.

source.place: Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), naturality applied to the augmentation; Tag 05SU

proof.text: For an augmentation-compatible map of the bar-resolution sequences, step 3 gives the commuting boundary square already at the presheaf-complex level. After colimit the resulting maps are maps of the degreewise exact $K$-sequences, so step 3 gives their boundary square in $D(R)$. Conjugating by the $m$'s and using step 7 gives the asserted square with the derived boundaries. For reindexing along $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$, a map $B_{\mathcal E}(F)\to u^{-1}B_{\mathcal D}(G)$ followed at every $U$ by the target colimit cocone gives $C_{\mathcal E}B_{\mathcal E}(F)\to C_{\mathcal D}B_{\mathcal D}(G)$, by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Applied to a morphism of the three sequences these maps commute with both arrows, hence again give a map of short exact $K$-sequences; the same cone calculation applies in $\operatorname{Mod}_R$. In the adjunct description, $u_!$ is the left adjoint to precomposition. Its bar terms and the source and target colimit terms have the acyclicity and boundedness needed for their derived comparisons by the explicit reindexing hypotheses. No exactness of $u_!$ on arbitrary sequences, or preservation of quasi-isomorphisms by ordinary colimit, is being used.

source.place: Tag 08PH (example-morphism-categories), induced maps on complexes; Tag 0152, naturality

proof.text: For a ring map $R_0\to R$, restriction of scalars changes only the scalar action. Kernels, images, quotients and finite sums are the identical underlying groups with restricted action. Thus it is exact, takes the displayed short exact sequences to short exact sequences, and preserves cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms. It also preserves shifts, the cone differential, $q$, $-\operatorname{pr}$ and the contraction $h$, since all their underlying group maps are unchanged. It therefore descends through the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], takes the roof $Q(-\operatorname{pr})(Qq)^{-1}$ to the identical roof over $R_0$, and preserves every equality in steps 3, 6 and 7. This proves the final clause after exact restriction of the asserted complexes, maps and derived comparisons; no flatness assumption is needed.
